tasks.title: Concurrent cell prepares keep invalidating each other's readiness validation
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (design choice). Seen 2026-10-31 on Portswood Rec (53,-42) with neighbour sessions preparing 52,-42/52,-43: `prepare --apply` on one cell changed the readiness revision of neighbouring cells, so a separate prepare then apply was refused 'validation stale' four times; builders had to chain prepare && apply in one shell command. Revision = content_id([POLICY, facts revision, plan_identity]) in lib/journal/cell_readiness.py; I did not find which input changes (suspect vector-map extract rewrite or neighbour plan notes). Questions: should validation of cell A depend on neighbour state at all? Should apply refresh validation itself under the lock? Decide, then fix.

tasks.title: prepare --apply records a duplicate plan_feature on every run (ambiguous legacy plan warning)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. On 53,-42 repeated `prepare --apply` added a second plan `houses_brickfield_road` for the same 6 houses already planned as houses_brickfield_road_w176633174, with warning 'ambiguous legacy plan ... no readable handoff spec'; a duplicate `houses_kitchener_road` (bare id from the 2026-10-29 build in row -43) also showed planned in 53,-42. I dismissed both with dismiss-feature. Decide whether prepare should skip groups already covered by a spec-backed plan, and how legacy bare ids should be matched.

tasks.title: Feature builds across a cell edge silently invalidate a finished neighbour and may generate ghost cells
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (policy). Applying houses_kitchener_road_w176634502 (footprint z -5382..-5343) reached 5 blocks into finished cell 53,-43 and marked its trees/decor stale (trees=False, decor=False). An earlier apply also generated a lidar ghost cell at 56,-40 (230k blocks, 'ghost-ground' journal seq 620) that the user did not ask for. Decide: warn/confirm before an apply touches a done neighbour; keep or drop frontier ghost generation on feature applies; whether edge fringe (roof overhang) should invalidate trees/decor at all.

tasks.title: reapply_feature refuses legacy house builds with no recorded builder; house_build apply bypasses the guard
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. houses_kitchener_road_w176658416 could not be reapplied (reapply_feature: no available recorded builder). At the owner's request I applied its old spec directly with house_build.py --apply under the lock (31905 positions, 0 mismatches), which bypasses the legacy-builder refusal and still leaves no recorded builder. Decide whether to backfill builder records for legacy spec-backed features (links #225, #228) so reapply works, and whether direct spec apply should be allowed for them.

tasks.title: World provider osm_extract.py: ogr2ogr ran without OSM_CONFIG_FILE; duplicates lib/sources
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. In worlds/southampton-build/providers/geofabrik-hampshire/osm_extract.py run_ogr2ogr passed no --config OSM_CONFIG_FILE, so GDAL 3.13's default schema (no `amenity` on points) failed the furniture preset and blocked `prepare --apply`. The world provider duplicates the presets and run_ogr2ogr in lib/sources/geofabrik_provider.py; decide whether to delete the copy and call the tool one. Also: manifest hints from prepare (`ref_manifest.py add ...` for prepared-53--42 and prepared-54--42, 52,-42, 52,-43) were not run.

tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Pitched roofs step in half blocks (slabs) where the lidar rises by half a block (I-019)
tasks.notes:
Serves I-019 (pitched roofs built from full blocks, no stairs or slabs; snags S-024, S-068, S-069). I-009 and its Kiddle snags (S-047, S-067) stay with #299: a float height does not change the 3x3 ridge peak.

Cause (measured 2026-11-16, read-only; the figures are from that run, not re-run by the reviewer). Zoned features take roof heights from the lidar provider's `mc_heights` (via `lidar_provider.mc_heights`, called in `_load_zone_grids`, lib/builds/feature_build.py ~1449-1473). The provider's default rounds every DSM/DTM sample to a whole metre; its float option returns unrounded heights and NaN for no-data. `_load_zone_grids` does not pass it, so every DSM value reaching `zone_ridge_half_steps` and `pitched_roof_states` is an integer. On west_w34391673 all 2019 median DSM cells have fractional part 0; the half-step histograms of West, Kiddle (w146985470) and w33830050 only ever have even keys; the West dry run plans 0 slabs and 313 full-brick roof tops. The odd half-step path that places slabs (#207, #209) therefore never fires on real data. Code read confirms that the regularising steps allow odd steps, so a float input would reach the slab path. Not verified: whether floats give clean half-steps or lidar noise.

Change: keep `dsm` and `ground_y` exactly as now (zone snapping, readable mask, footprints, ground heights and the injected `zone_data` format are unchanged). Add a second, float DSM grid (key `dsm_fine`, optional in `zone_data`) fetched through one wrapper in lib/sources/lidar_provider.py (for example `mc_heights_float`) that asks the provider for its float option and falls back to the integer grid on a TypeError (a provider without the option). NaN no-data stays unreadable. Use `dsm_fine` only in the 3x3 median passed to `zone_ridge_half_steps` (~line 1519) for pitched labels; flat labels unchanged. Say in the code comment why the wrapper exists. Other callers that already ask for floats without a fallback (lib/layers/outbuildings.py, lib/journal/readiness_evidence.py) are left alone. Write "the provider's float option" in code and text; no vendor names.

Risk to test first: zone levels are authored whole metres, so a true eave at 44.6 m against level 44 gives 1 half-step across the whole deck once any ridge in the zone exceeds the flat tolerance. Check the per-zone rise histogram and the share of cells at 1 half-step outside the ridge rows.

Tests (synthetic, via `zone_data` and `zone_ridge_half_steps` called directly): a 1.5 m rise above the eave gives 3 half-steps and plans a slab course; whole-metre input behaves exactly as today; NaN cells are unreadable, not zero; a provider without the option falls back to integers; `dsm` and `ground_y` identical with and without `dsm_fine`.

Check (read-only first): dry run `python3 scripts/feature_build.py --world southampton-build <spec>` (no --apply) for west_w34391673, w146985470 and w33830050 (specs under worlds/southampton-build/site/builds/). Report the half-step histogram before and after. Require: odd keys appear, West plans more than 0 slabs, 0 ridge-jog failures, 0 stair-shape mismatches, no odd step beside a 0 step more than 2 half-steps apart, and few 1-half-step cells outside ridge rows. If noise speckles the roof, stop, file a smoothing task and do not ship. The live rebuilds are the orchestrator's job.

Snag checks (after a rebuild): S-069 West's roof tops off with bottom-half slabs at half-block steps, not full blocks beside stairs; S-068 the same on David Kiddle (w146985470); S-024 West's pitched roof uses stairs and slabs.

Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, lib/builds/test_feature_build.py, lib/sources/lidar_provider.py (and its test). Not a stretch unless the noise check fails.

tasks.title: Trees and decor stand on lidar terrain height, not the live surface (a roof) (I-046, I-038)
tasks.notes:
Serves "Trees stand on a roof" (I-046; two snags: two trees on West's roof and two on a flat roof near Retail, cell 48,-44) and the decor-on-an-overhanging-roof issue (I-038; S-064, S-066). Owner direction (2026-11-16): the cure for a roof overhang is to build trees and decor on the true ground level, not to remove them and not to skip the column; building them from game-world heights rather than lidar heights "is asking for trouble". Trees may use the air around a feature (leaves can hang in air beside or above a roof or wall) but may not replace any block a feature owns. Precedent: #167 (ground from lidar terrain), #172, #204 (door floors from lidar ground), #206 (the veto this task replaces).

Cause (code read; the measurement was not replayed in a test).
- Trees: lib/layers/trees_layer.py `candidate()` takes the trunk base from `surface_y(world, x, z)`, the live top non-plant block, so a roof counts as ground. The 'feature zone' rule (`fp` / `ground_cols`) is skipped for evidenced crowns (aerial, surveyed, extra: `observed`), so an evidenced crown over a roof is planted on it. Measured 2026-11-16: a trees+decor redo of 48,-44 (readback 0 mismatches) left exactly the same 215 oak_leaves and 5 oak_log beside West's roof, so a fresh pass places them there again. Not verified: how each of those crowns was sourced. The trees layer has no lidar terrain grid today; its lidar use is the canopy (nDSM) snapping only.
- Decor: lib/layers/decor_layer.py also stands on `surface_y`; since #206 it refuses a column whose live surface is more than 2 blocks above terrain (`above_lidar_ground`, reason 'above lidar ground'). That removes the item; it does not move it to the ground.

Change.
1. One shared helper (for example `ground_at(world, lidar_hm, x, z)` in surface_probe) returns the terrain block Y for a column and the block at that Y. Trunk base, decor base and every material, water, carriageway and 'uneven trunk ground' check read the block at terrain Y through it, never `surface_y` (over a roof `surface_y`, `column_ground_kind` and the carriageway test all return the roof block). Both layers use it.
2. The block at terrain Y must be solid, unowned ground; otherwise the item is unplaced with the reason 'no ground at terrain' (no floating trunk or decor). Warm the prefetch for the terrain-Y reads (#110/#263 stalls).
3. The trees layer loads the terrain grid once into `TreeInputs` (decor already gets it from `reference_world().heightmap(cell)` in plan_cell), injectable in tests like the other inputs.
4. A crown or decor body may fill air blocks anywhere, including beside or above a feature. A voxel on a block owned by a feature (`owned`, `neighbour_owned`) or by another pass mask is dropped (leaves) or makes the item unplaced (trunk, decor body): never overwritten. These checks already exist; keep them and test them. Open choice for the owner: a feature's margin air counts as owned, so leaves are dropped there too; accept that, or exempt owned air for leaves.
5. An item is unplaced only where a feature-owned block stands in its own column between terrain and the item's top (for example directly under a low roof). The report lists it with the reason 'feature above terrain'. It is never moved onto the roof.
6. Remove the #206 skip-the-column veto. Sites to change: `above_lidar_ground` and its docstrings ('lidar veto'), `may_join_at`, `place_furniture`, `place_barriers_from_plan` (decor_layer.py), and the 'above lidar ground' and 'below lidar ground' refusals in `place_outbuildings` (which already builds from terrain: align it to the helper). Convert the tests: test_decor_layer.py (~249, 260, 580-590), test_outbuildings.py (~254), test_layer_reports.py (~21). Update docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md (~67). The fix text for I-038 on the world side is the orchestrator's to update.
7. Where lidar terrain is missing for a column, keep today's behaviour and say so in the report.

Files: lib/layers/trees_layer.py, lib/layers/decor_layer.py, lib/layers/outbuildings.py, decor_plan.py if the unplaced reasons live there, surface_probe (or the module that holds it), docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md and the tests above.

Tests (synthetic world): a crown over a roof with open ground beneath grows from the terrain; a tree whose crown overlaps a feature-owned roof block keeps the roof block and drops those leaves; a trunk column blocked by a feature block is unplaced with 'feature above terrain'; leaves fill air beside a wall; decor on terrain under an overhang is placed at terrain height; owned and masked blocks are never overwritten; a floating base is 'no ground at terrain'; missing terrain falls back to today's behaviour; the helper is read through for water and carriageway checks.

Check (read-only first): `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_trees_layer --only test_decor_layer --only test_outbuildings --only test_layer_reports`. Then dry runs of the two layers separately (a decor dry run after an unapplied trees step cannot see the new trees): `python3 scripts/trees_layer.py --world southampton-build --cell 48,-44` and `python3 scripts/decor_layer.py --world southampton-build --cell 48,-44` (no --apply). Report counts of trees and decor moved to terrain, unplaced with each new reason, and any planned block at a feature-owned position (must be 0). After a live redo (orchestrator's job): a block scan of x6200-6226, z-5610..-5586, y58-90 shows no oak_log above the West roof line.

Snag checks (after a trees+decor redo of 48,-44): the two trees on West's roof stand on the ground beside or below it, or are absent only where a feature blocks the trunk column; the two trees on the flat roof near Retail likewise; no hedge or decor on a roof; no leaf or log replaces a building block.

tasks.title: Smooth roof half-steps from the provider's float option so #300 can ship (I-019)
tasks.notes:
Continues #300 (pitched roofs step in half blocks, I-019; snags S-024, S-068, S-069). #300 stays todo and ships together with this task.

State: the float DSM change is written and committed as WIP on branch `task/300-roof-slabs` (commit 10fcfcd, NOT merged, not shippable as it stands): `mc_heights_float` in lib/sources/lidar_provider.py with integer fallback on TypeError, `dsm_fine` in `_load_zone_grids`, 3x3 median of `dsm_fine` into `zone_ridge_half_steps`, five synthetic tests; test_feature_build and test_lidar_provider pass. Continue on that branch.

Why it stopped (dry runs 2026-11-16, southampton-build): odd half-step keys now appear and slabs are planned (West 0 -> 450, Kiddle 0 -> 417, w33830050 0 -> 935), 0 odd steps beside 0 steps more than 2 apart, clean contiguous pitch bands on West and Kiddle. But: (1) zone levels are authored whole metres and true decks sit about 0.5 m above them, so flat decks become blocks of 1-half-step slabs: 1-half-step cells with no neighbour above 1 are West 218, Kiddle 309, w33830050 398; (2) isolated odd cells (differ from all four neighbours) are West 108, Kiddle 15, w33830050 159, none before; (3) w33830050 gets 1 ridge jog (one-cell shift, z row 6388 y 61) and its dry run refuses the plan; it built before.

Change: after `zone_ridge_half_steps` on `dsm_fine`: (1) calibrate each zone's flat deck against its authored whole-metre level, so a deck 0.5 m above its level does not become 1-half-step slabs; (2) drop isolated odd half-steps by snapping a lone odd cell to its neighbours before regularising; (3) keep ridge rows from shifting by one cell between rows.

Check (dry run, no --apply) on west_w34391673, w146985470, w33830050: 0 ridge jogs on all three; at most 1 stair-shape mismatch on West (as today); a small count of 1-half-step cells with no neighbour above 1; odd keys and slabs still present on West; isolated odd cells near 0. Report the histograms before and after. Tests: synthetic, a lone odd cell is snapped; a deck 0.5 m above its level stays flat; a ridge does not jog. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py and its test. Write "the provider's float option" in code and text; no vendor names.

tasks.title: Decor, trees and ground dry runs on a built cell understate the plan and overwrite tracked reports
tasks.notes:
Found in #244 (2026-11-16). `python3 scripts/decor_layer.py --world W --cell C` (dry run) on a cell that is already built treats the cell's own decor mask as blocked, so it understates the plan: on 53,-43 it reported 305 blocks instead of about 2,716 and every front hedge failed as 'blocked by live or owned block'. A real rebuild undoes first, so only the dry run misleads. Also, the dry run overwrote two tracked world files (the 53,-43 decor report and preview).
Change: on a dry run, treat the cell's own decor mask as undone (as the redo path does), or print a clear warning when the cell has a decor mask; and write a dry run's report and preview to the verification folder only, never over a tracked world file. Tests: a built cell's dry-run count matches a clean plan; the tracked report is not rewritten. Same check for trees_layer.py and ground if they share the behaviour (say which do). Note from #301: trees_layer.py's dry run also crashes in `preview()` when the plan is empty; fix it here.
